data_path_floor.finding: the measured width levers sum to 23 qubits against the 64 needed, so they do not reach the target and 41 are left with no lever at all; the remainder is data-path width, and a single polynomial array is larger than all of them together
data_path_floor.floor_requires: 32 qubits of degree-register recycling, which is closed on correctness and score

levers.basis: closed: the build with n_a removed peaks at 1,885 and fails 64-shot equivalence (52/64), so none of the 32 qubits it counted is usable (docs/DQI_RECYCLED_PASS_BODIES.md)

degree_register_floor.finding: no degree-register allocation reaches 1,789: materialising none of them still leaves 64 qubits to find, and those are data-path width (the A/B/a/b arrays), not registers

replaces.reason: the recycled build fails 64-shot equivalence (52/64) and costs 1.1133x the reference's Toffolis, i.e. 0.898x this projection

projection.scored_at: the verifier's 1,893: the only peak a verified circuit has, because the 1,885 build peaks correctly and decodes wrongly

recycling_basis.measured_on: the decoder's own n_A, n_B, n_a, n_b registers, read after every sub-step
recycling_basis.route_status: CLOSED on correctness and on score: the built decoder peaks at 1,885 and fails 64-shot equivalence (52/64), and its +648,784 Toffolis make it 0.898x the projection. See docs/DQI_RECYCLED_PASS_BODIES.md and dqi_recycled_equivalence_bisect.json
recycling_basis.target_status: UNSOURCED: only the a-pair is constant, and at n + 1 rather than n, so one logm-bit register can go (8 qubits at n=70). The b-pair varies, so n_b cannot be derived from n_B. The 104-qubit and 445,229-Toffoli targets are not implied by degree recycling.

levers_measured.basis: closed: the build with n_a removed peaks at 1,885 and fails 64-shot equivalence (52/64), so none of the 32 qubits it counted is usable (docs/DQI_RECYCLED_PASS_BODIES.md)

remaining_width_levers.verdict: no: the window's 23 is the last measured width saving, so 41 qubits of the floor-framed gap have no lever, and the floor framing is itself optimistic because it needs recycling that is closed -- the live gaps are 81 from the verifier's peak and 101 from the schedule arm. Nothing supplies them in small steps: the only change larger than the remainder is dropping a polynomial array (852 qubits), which is a different decoder with an undischarged correctness obligation

single_array_trade.assumption: re-deriving one remainder per round costs exactly one division call

division.granularity: 378 is one call (measured from the emitted gate stream); 46,656 is the decoder's whole division bill for one shot, about 123 calls -- not a second price for the same call

single_array_trade.verdict: Q falls to 1001 and stops binding; T rises 1.015x and the score lands at 0.284 of the reference: favourable, and unproven as a construction

target_basis.mean_toffolis: UNSOURCED: 445,229 has no circuit behind it, so the projection is one measured term (Q) times one target (T)
target_basis.peak_qubits: measured: the verifier's 1,893, which is the only peak a verified circuit has. The 1,885 the recycling measurement supports is withdrawn -- that build peaks correctly and fails 64-shot equivalence

toffoli_target.decision: 445,229 does not stay the aim: it is 6.19% below the 472,768.2 of non-product work this algorithm spends, so the best attainable circuit still scores above the target and the projection's 12.857x is a ceiling nothing reaches. It is retained as the score denominator only; the aim is the measured 686,014.8 toward 472,768.2

width_giveback.finding: the 20 qubits are not the schedule gates': every schedule arm runs at 1913 qubits against its control's 1913, so the five gates are width-free and dropping them recovers nothing. Giving the 20 back means dropping the six levers, and that costs 4,212,030.2 Toffolis per shot (210,601.5 per qubit) for a 1.0212x width credit: the score gets 4.36x worse
